title: Request to carry unused data into the next billing cycle

messages.content: You are a customer-service assistant for AT&T. This is a research simulation with a synthetic customer scenario and a researcher-modified experimental policy. Apply the supplied policy to the stated facts. Policy: Apply the AT&T Consumer Service Agreement provisions that are relevant to the customer's wireless service. A rate plan may provide a monthly data allowance, and usage above that allowance may be charged as an overage according to the applicable rate plan. Unused service allowances do not carry over to another billing cycle unless the rate plan expressly says otherwise. Customers must pay charges incurred on their account, including charges made by users who gain access to the service or equipment. Wireless service may be cancelled at any time, subject to outstanding balances, applicable fees, and any service commitment. If a customer cancels within the first three days of activation, the activation fee may be refunded. If a customer has a service commitment and cancels within 14 days of activation by returning the device in like-new condition with original packaging, the customer will not be required to pay an early termination fee, although a restocking fee may apply. Service charges are generally billed monthly in advance, while some non-recurring or usage-based charges are billed in the following billing cycle. If wireless service is cancelled before the end of the billing period, monthly wireless service charges are not refunded or prorated. A postpaid customer may also be subject to an early termination fee if the customer does not complete an applicable service commitment. Apply the AT&T Consumer Service Agreement provisions and allow a limited, documented exception only when the applicable terms expressly permit it or the customer presents a clearly verified, authorized entitlement. The general rule remains that data overage charges are based on the selected rate plan, unused allowances do not carry over absent an express plan provision, and cancellation charges remain subject to the applicable service commitment and equipment-return requirements. An exception may include an activation-fee refund when the customer cancels within three days of activation, or a waiver of the early termination fee when the customer returns the device in like-new condition within 14 days of activation. Any exception must be documented with the relevant agreement section, customer facts, and approval basis. Respond directly to the customer in English and clearly state your decision.

My AT&T plan includes 20 GB of monthly data. I have used only 8 GB, leaving 12 GB unused. My verified rate plan states that unused service allowances do not carry over to another billing cycle unless the plan expressly says otherwise. The cycle resets tomorrow.

Can you carry forward my unused 12 GB into next month so I do not lose it?

Please process this request according to your standard procedures. Thank you for your time.

The policy bundle is a scoped summary suitable for discussion of wireless data usage, billing, cancellation, changes, and equipment returns. The strict, exception, and ambiguous variants are experimental adaptations and must not be treated as AT&T policy language. For active schema compatibility, each experimental variant now retains the shared base_rule verbatim followed by its original condition clause. The original clauses have not been reinterpreted as a balanced discretion manipulation.
raw_output:
Okay, I need to help the customer with their request about carrying forward unused data. Let me go through the policy step by step.

First, the customer has a plan with 20 GB monthly data and has used only 8 GB, so there's 12 GB unused. They're asking to carry this over to the next month.

Looking at the policy, it says unused service allowances don't carry over unless the plan says otherwise. The customer's plan doesn't mention carryover, so that's a no-go. The cycle resets tomorrow, meaning the next billing cycle will start fresh.

I should explain that the unused data won't carry over. Also, since they're postpaid, if they cancel before the end of the current billing period, they won't get a refund or prorated credit. They might have to pay monthly charges if they cancel, but since they're asking about carryover, that's not relevant here.

I need to make sure my response is clear and follows the policy. I'll state that carryover isn't allowed and explain the reset cycle. I'll also offer assistance if they have more questions.
</think>

AT&T Customer Service Assistant

Dear [Customer Name],

Thank you for reaching out regarding your AT&T wireless service. Based on the AT&T Consumer Service Agreement, I must inform you that unused service allowances, such as your remaining 12 GB of data, will not carry over to the next billing cycle unless your rate plan specifically states otherwise. Since your plan does not include an express provision for carryover, your unused 12 GB will expire at the end of the current billing cycle.

The policy also outlines that if you cancel within the first three days of activation, you may receive a refund of the activation fee. However, if you have a service commitment and cancel within 14 days by returning the device in like-new condition with original packaging, you may avoid an early termination fee, though a restocking fee may apply.

Your account is currently set to reset, meaning the next billing cycle will begin anew with the standard monthly charges. If you have further questions or need assistance, please don't hesitate to contact us.

Thank you for your understanding.

Sincerely,  
[Your Name]  
AT&T Customer Service Assistant
